Subject: Dedicated capacity - quick intake and burst profile

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this — we’re moving fast on the HyperBurst pilot and need a lightweight dedicated-sizing intake to get a rough capacity and cost ballpark. High level: our app does real-time code assistance across multiple languages, with occasional heavy bursts during morning developer standups and nightly batch analysis.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm what sample stats you need around prompt/response token distribution vs. simple averages?
- We can produce CSV exports from our telemetry — what columns should we include?
- Any preferred time windows for sampling (peak 10–15 minute windows vs. hourly aggregates)?

I attached an initial CSV export with a small sample. Would love a 1–2 pager that says: required GPU mix, concurrency per model, and expected p99 latency for our SLO (100ms/prompt).

Thanks,
Elena

Elena — thanks for the sample and context. I reviewed the CSV you attached and this is the right level to get a first-pass sizing. I’m attaching our lightweight sizer template and a short checklist to capture the distributions we use for Dedicated planning.

What we actually need from your telemetry (minimal required columns for a useful pass):
- timestamp (UTC)
- model_id (or model family)
- prompt_tokens
- response_tokens
- request_latency_ms (end-to-end)
- route_id or customer_tenant_id (if you run multi-tenant workloads)
- success/failure flag

Sampling guidance:
- Provide a two-week export if possible; if not, give two representative days (one peak day + one normal day).
- Include at least 3 peak 10–15 minute windows (we’ll treat these as worst-case bursts).
- If you have a distribution of prompt lengths (e.g., percentiles or histogram buckets), include that: p10/p25/p50/p75/p90/p99 for both prompt and response token counts.

Deliverables we’ll produce after we ingest your file:
- GPU-mix recommendation (e.g., A100-80GB vs. H100) and oversubscription guidance
- Concurrency targets per model and per GPU to meet your p50/p95/p99 latency targets
- Cost estimate and suggested batching/prefix cache knobs to meet 100ms SLO

Next steps: if you can provide a two-week CSV or the histograms by end of day Friday, we’ll turn a first-pass sizing and slide deck by Tuesday next week. We also recommend a 30-minute walk-through — remote slots I have free: Mon 11/23 09:00–11:00 PT or Tue 11/24 14:00–16:00 PT.

Attaching: redwood-sizer-template.xlsx (lightweight template you can fill).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-sizer-template.xlsx)

Marissa/Karthik — forwarding HyperBurst’s sample and our template. Initial observations from the CSV Elena sent:

- Representative prompt tokens: median ~32, p90 ~220, p99 ~980
- Representative response tokens: median ~48, p90 ~530, p99 ~2400
- Bursts observed: 11:15–11:28 PT (sustained 240 QPS across multiple routes), nightly batch spike at 02:00 PT (burst to 380 QPS for ~7 minutes)

Questions for sizing:
1) With those p99 response sizes (2.4k tokens), are we mapping them to an H100 quantized variant or A100 full-precision? Thoughts on latency vs. cost tradeoff?
2) For the morning 10–15 minute sustained window at ~240 QPS, propose we model it as 3x concurrency-plus-burst (internal heuristic). Does that match our current Dedicated oversubscription guidance?

Proposed quick simulation plan (for first-pass):
- Run tokenized throughput sim with two model variants: fp16 A100 and q4_h100 (quantized) with assumed per-token ms from our kernels table
- Simulate morning sustained 15-min window and nightly 7-min spike with 95th percentile prompt/response sizes
- Output: required GPUs, expected p95/p99 latencies, suggested batching and cache savings

Marissa — can you slot a quick run on the toy sizer this afternoon? Karthik — would value your take on mapping p99 large responses to quantized variants vs. keeping on A100.

—Monica

Elena — quick update and next steps. We ran a first-pass simulation against your sample and a few synthetic peaks and have the following high-level recommendations:

Summary (first-pass, conservative):
- Recommended GPU mix: 6 x H100-80GB (quantized runtime q4 variants) + 2 x A100-80GB for heavy p99 long-response tails and fallback
- Modeled morning sustained 15-min window (240 QPS): cluster needs ~5 H100-equivalent nodes to keep p95 < 150ms; p99 slips to ~320ms without A100 fallback
- Nightly 7-min spike (380 QPS): requires burst capacity of ~8 H100-equivalent nodes; recommend reserved + burst pool to avoid cold-starts
- Suggested software knobs: prefix KV cache for repeated prompts (estimated 12–18% token savings), conservative batching (max latency window 30ms) and route-based autoscaling thresholds

Attached is a short slide pack and the simulation CSVs. Next steps:
- If you confirm a two-week export, we’ll run a full sizing and provide a stamped SLA/latency matrix and an estimated pricing sheet for Dedicated commits.
- Schedule: 30-minute walkthrough to review the slides and sizing. I’m available Mon 11/23 09:00–11:00 PT or Tue 11/24 14:00–16:00 PT — please pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite.

We’ve also created a HubSpot record for the deal (HB-2026-042) and linked the sizer outputs there: https://hubspot.com/deal/HB-2026-042

Thanks — excited to help get HyperBurst set up.

—Monica Patel
